To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the temperature dependence (Ea) of phytoplankten metabolism decreases under N-limited conditions, compared to nutrient-replete conditions, and (ii) this reduced temperature dependence is explained by the increased temperature sensitivity of enzyme kinetics under N-limitation.

1) The temperature sensitivity of photosynthesis, respiration and growth rates decreases with nutrient limitation, 2) The temperature sensitivity (activation energy) of maximum photosynthesis and respiration rates increases with temperature, 3) Temperature sensitivity (activation energy of growth rate) is not constant with temperature, but increases with increasing temperature, and 4) Temperature sensitivity of growth rate (activation energy) increases with nutrient limitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of temperature on phytoplankton growth rates, which is a key parameter for the understanding of phytoplanktons’ contribution to climate change.
how nutrient limitation affects the temperature dependence of metabolic processes in phytoplankton.
the effects of temperature and nutrient limitation on the metabolic rates of marine phytoplankton.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temperature dependence of metabolic processes is a function of the nutrient status of the organisms.

the temperature sensitivity of phyto- and zooplankton metabolic rates is reduced under nutrient limitation, which is consistent with the idea that nutrient limitation is a major factor suppressing phytoplankton growth in the ocean.
temperature sensitivity of phyto-plankton metabolic rates depends on nutrient supply.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

nutrient limitation suppresses the effect of temperature on metabolic rates in phytoplankton, and therefore the warming of surface ocean waters may have a limited effect on phytoplankton productivity and carbon sequestration in the ocean.
nutrient limitation suppresses the effect of rising temperatures on the metabolism of marine phytoplankton, and this effect is consistent across different species.
the temperature sensitivity of phytoplancton metabolic rates is not universal but rather dependent on the nutrient availability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nutrient limitation can suppress the temperature dependence of metabolic processes, with implications for the response of marine ecosystems to climate change.
the response of marine primary production to climate warming will be modulated by nutrient availability.
the temperature dependence of metabolism is not a fixed property of organisms, but is rather determined by the prevailing environmental conditions.
